policySet.name: gspp-archetype-baseline
policySet.description: Azure Policy effects chosen per archetype by the enforcement decision rule in resources/doctrine.md. Groups are GS++ requirement IDs; group category is the modal verb. Candidate mapping, not a compliance statement.

azure-policy.evidence: Azure Policy compliance state; policyDefinitionGroupNames name the requirement

entra.evidence: identity-provider configuration export and sign-in reports; not an Azure Policy result

data-catalogue.evidence: data inventory and classification report from a data catalogue (for example Microsoft Purview)

provider-attestation.evidence: contract clause and provider attestation (for example a C5 report)

process-owner.evidence: dated attestation by the process owner

named-decision.evidence: decision with justification, approved in a reviewed pull request

ARCH.5.1.paraphrase: Network architecture restricts connections between IT systems.

ARCH.5.2.paraphrase: IT systems have no direct path to the public network.

ASST.2.1.paraphrase: An inventory of information and related assets is documented.

ASST.2.4.paraphrase: Data is assigned a protection-need class.

BER.4.6.paraphrase: Application functions reachable without prior authentication are documented.

BER.5.8.paraphrase: Interfaces that external parties could reach require phishing-resistant multi-factor sign-in.

BES.2.2.paraphrase: Procurement documents the jurisdiction and data location of each cloud service.

BES.2.3.paraphrase: Procurement may agree jurisdiction and data location with the provider.

BES.4.8.2.paraphrase: The cloud contract provides for independent third-party evidence of conformity.

DET.3.1.paraphrase: Applications log security-relevant events and keep them for a set period (parameter).

DET.3.1.8.paraphrase: Use of privileged functions, including switching them on or off, is logged.

DET.3.2.paraphrase: Events from cloud services may feed the organisation's own audit log.

DET.5.3.paraphrase: A vulnerability-scanning procedure, including evaluation and treatment, is established.

DET.5.10.2.paraphrase: Missing updates are detected by an automated mechanism (parameter).

DLS.3.1.1.paraphrase: A service provider's security is verified by audit, certificate or equivalent evidence at a set interval (parameters).

GC.3.1.1.paraphrase: Legal obligations that affect information processing are analysed.

KONF.11.8.paraphrase: Applications may encrypt data worth protecting at rest.

KONF.14.1.paraphrase: Applications encrypt network transport to a recognised standard (parameter).

KONF.14.1.1.paraphrase: Applications disable unencrypted and weak network connections.

NOT.4.3.paraphrase: Application data is backed up at a set interval (parameter).

NOT.4.12.paraphrase: At least one backup copy may be held in a second, distant region.

NOT.4.16.1.paraphrase: Restore is tested on representative samples at a set interval (parameter).

STM.2.1.7.paraphrase: Requirements that arise from external obligations are added to the requirement package.

STM.5.1.paraphrase: Requirements with parameters are given concrete values.

UMS.5.1.paraphrase: Exceptions are authorised by a responsible person or role (parameter).

UMS.5.2.paraphrase: Exceptions are documented with a justification.

themes.note: Data location follows from an external obligation (law or contract), so STM.2.1.7 adds it to the package and no exemption can waive it. The allowed regions are a parameter (STM.5.1).

allowedLocations.description: Regions the external obligation allows (STM.5.1 value).

themes.note: The KONF.14.1 parameter (a recognised standard) is assigned as TLS 1.2 or later over HTTPS only.

policies.displayName: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
Storage accounts should have the specified minimum TLS version

minimumTlsVersion.description: Recognised standard for transport encryption (KONF.14.1 parameter, STM.5.1 value).

themes.note: Online serves the internet by design, so its archetype record carries the standing deviation and Azure Policy only reports. Shown for storage accounts; the shared mapping lists further services.

policies.displayName: Storage accounts should disable public network access

themes.note: The definition checks that a network security group is attached to each subnet, not that its rules restrict anything; it reads a Defender for Cloud assessment. The lab has no virtual network, so the policy shows no applicable resources.

policies.displayName: Subnets should be associated with a Network Security Group

themes.note: The requirement asks to document unauthenticated functions. The policy goes further and switches anonymous blob access off, so an approved exemption becomes the documentation (inferred mapping).

policies.displayName: Configure your Storage account public access to be disallowed

themes.note: Platform encryption at rest is always on; this KANN adds infrastructure (double) encryption, selected only by Confidential Corp.

policies.displayName: Storage accounts should have infrastructure encryption

themes.note: Shown for Key Vault audit logs. The DET.3.1 parameter (a set period) is the workspace retention, which Azure Policy does not set.

policies.displayName: Enable logging by category group for Key vaults (microsoft.keyvault/vaults) to Log Analytics

logAnalyticsWorkspaceId.description: Resource ID of the Log Analytics workspace that receives security logs.

themes.note: Privileged control-plane operations are in the Azure activity log. The platform team assigns the built-in definition that streams it to a workspace once per subscription or management group, so it is outside this initiative and the same for every archetype.

The platform assignment of activity-logging also feeds the organisation's workspace, so every archetype selects this KANN. A separate theme because a KANN deviates by archetype change, never by exemption.
Shown for virtual machines; the lab has none, so the policy shows no applicable resources. PaaS services are patched by the provider.

policies.displayName: Machines should be configured to periodically check for missing system updates

themes.note: Shown for virtual machines; the lab has none, so the policy shows no applicable resources. The interval parameter is the backup policy schedule.

policies.displayName: Azure Backup should be enabled for Virtual Machines

themes.note: Shown for storage accounts. The definition offers Audit only, so an archetype that selects this KANN cannot block locally redundant storage: an enforcement gap. Where a backup vault holds the copy, its storage redundancy is the evidence.

policies.displayName: Geo-redundant storage should be enabled for Storage Accounts

themes.note: A restore test is an activity, not a resource property.

Sign-in policy lives in the identity provider; Azure Policy cannot see it. A built-in definition can demand multi-factor sign-in for Azure Resource Manager writes, which covers neither external interfaces nor other privileges.
Inventory and protection-need class describe data, not resource configuration.
The requirement is a procedure. A scanner can supply findings; it does not establish the procedure.
Confidential Corp selects this KANN: jurisdiction and data location are agreed in the contract.
Third-party evidence such as a C5 or ISO/IEC 27001 report is a contract and review matter, not a resource property.
Produces the external obligations that bind other themes, such as residency.
Every exemption and attestation exception needs a named approver and a justification (challenge 3).
